**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small serving of stir-fried or sautéed leafy greens (looks like kale or collard/mustard greens) with thin carrot slices and possibly some garlic or onion, on a white plate. Photographed from above (near top-down).

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** White plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side-plate size). Radius 10 cm, area = 3.14 × 10² ≈ 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (a) cooked dark leafy greens, (b) carrot pieces, (c) a little oil/sauce sheen and light aromatics (not clearly separable, folded into the greens).

**STEP 4 - Area:** The greens cover about 25% of the plate (the pile sits in the center, roughly 10 cm across). Greens ≈ 23% (≈72 cm²), carrot ≈ 2% (≈6 cm²). Total food ≈ 25%.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Greens: 72 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 216 ml (a loose, tall-ish pile). Carrot: 6 cm² × 0.5 cm ≈ 3 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cooked greens: 216 ml × 0.15 g/ml ≈ 32 g. Carrot: 3 ml × 0.6 ≈ 2 g. Oil/sauce sheen: ~2 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked leafy greens (sautéed, oil-free basis) ≈ 30 kcal/100 g → 32 g ≈ 10 kcal. Carrot ≈ 35 kcal/100 g → 2 g ≈ 1 kcal. Oil ≈ 880 kcal/100 g → 2 g ≈ 18 kcal. (Greens are typically cooked with some oil, so the added oil figure accounts for that.)

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A modest pile covering about a quarter of a side plate, around 35–40 g and about 30 kcal, is plausible. Visible food is small; no larger serving is assumed.

Total: about 36 g, about 30 kcal.
